feedback: The baseline result (iteration 0, score 54.37) is the evidence for this feedback. All 60 trials on oval, s-bend and slalom lost the line once, reached max_error of about 0.062 to 0.064 m, and went off track at 10 to 15 percent progress. rms_error and steering_oscillation were modest, so the failure is an abrupt line loss, not steady jitter. Widening the span to ±0.03 m is a sound response to that. The Integrator has also lowered base_speed and kp slightly in this iteration, so any change in result will be partly due to the controller and not only the geometry. Your off-track limit arithmetic should read max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.14/4) = max(0.06, 0.0475) = 0.06 m, not 0.0525 m, so body_width does not move the limit at this width. Do not treat that as a lever. Next race: if line_loss_events falls and progress rises, keep the ±0.03 m span and test the forward offset as a separate change. If line loss persists at ±0.03 m, the footprint is more likely the limit than the span, so test sensor_size 0.016 with the span held. Hold the wheel track, mass and body, because the evidence does not point at them.
requested_changes: Keep the ±0.03 m span and 15 mm spacing, and hold the forward offset at 0.05 m for this race so the span effect can be read alongside the controller change.
If line_loss_events is still about 1 per run after this race, test sensor_size 0.016 with the span unchanged, since larger footprints keep the 25 mm tape under a sensor for longer.
If steering_oscillation rises at speed after the span change, test a forward offset of about 0.03 m as a separate change, not together with a footprint change.
